notes: Reproduction by the MIKASA-Robo paper of π₀. Standard 5-task MIKASA-Robo protocol: 250 demos/task, 100 evaluation episodes/task at 128x128 RGB, end-effector control, averaged over 3 independent runs.

Non-standard MIKASA-Robo 4-task set (ShellGameTouch, InterceptMedium, TakeItBack, RememberShape5), not the standard 5-task VLA protocol; paper Avg.SR stored in suite_scores.reported_avg. Third-party reproduction reported in the FibVLA paper.

Reproduction by the MIKASA-Robo paper of the Decision Transformer baseline. The listed score is the arithmetic mean of the five canonical VLA tasks, reaggregated from the paper's 32-task offline-RL Table 8 rather than a separate VLA-protocol evaluation. The offline-RL setup uses 1,000 successful trajectories per task, two RGB camera views, sparse rewards, three training runs, and 100 evaluation episodes per run.

Reproduction by the MIKASA-Robo paper of the Recurrent Action Transformer with memory (RATE) baseline. The listed score is the arithmetic mean of the five canonical VLA tasks, reaggregated from the paper's 32-task offline-RL Table 8 rather than a separate VLA-protocol evaluation. The offline-RL setup uses 1,000 successful trajectories per task, two RGB camera views, sparse rewards, three training runs, and 100 evaluation episodes per run.

Generic Behavioral Cloning baseline (no specific source paper) reproduced by the MIKASA-Robo authors. The listed score is the arithmetic mean of the five canonical VLA tasks, reaggregated from the paper's 32-task offline-RL Table 8 rather than a separate VLA-protocol evaluation. The offline-RL setup uses 1,000 successful trajectories per task, two RGB camera views, sparse rewards, three training runs, and 100 evaluation episodes per run.

First-party result from the ELMUR paper. Standard 5-task MIKASA-Robo protocol with 3 independent training runs, 100 evaluation episodes per run with distinct seeds, paired RGB images (3x128x128) from static and wrist cameras, continuous 7-joint + gripper actions, binary sparse rewards.

First-party result from the μVLA paper (Cherepanov et al.); μVLA is a recurrent-memory LoRA fine-tune of OpenVLA-OFT (memory width m=64, TBPTT length K=2). overall_score is null: scores are from the non-standard 23-task MIKASA-Robo-VLA evaluation (Table 1), where the model is trained on a different 5-task mixture (RememberColor5, RememberShapeAndColor3x3, ShellGamePush, TakeItBack, InterceptMedium). Of the canonical 5 tasks, InterceptMedium (47) and RememberColor5 (93) are in-distribution while ShellGameTouch (0; trained on ShellGamePush instead), RememberColor3 (92) and RememberColor9 (41) are held-out generalization results — not comparable to standard-protocol rows. 100 evaluation episodes per task.

Standard 5-task MIKASA-Robo protocol: 250 demos/task at 128x128 RGB, end-effector control, 100 evaluation episodes/task, all 5 tasks jointly trained for 20k steps, single input frame per forward pass. Per-task scores and 44.4 average read from Table III; protocol confirmed standard (5-task, not the 4-task ELMUR variant) from the paper body, resolving the extract-stage 'unknown' flag.
